hints: Divide the total sum by $7$ and round to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Sum all seven plant heights:
$$\sum x = 4.2 + 5.1 + 6.3 + 4.8 + 5.6 + 6.0 + 4.9 = 36.9\text{ cm}$$

Divide by the sample size $n = 7$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{36.9}{7} \approx 5.2714 = 5.27\text{ cm (3 s.f.)}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sum the 7 values to obtain 36.9 cm.
Divide by 7 to obtain mean = 5.27 cm (or 36.9 / 7).

hints: Multiply the mean ($14$) by the number of scores ($8$) to find the total sum required.
Add the seven given scores and subtract from the total sum.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the required total for all 8 scores:
$$\text{Total} = n \times \bar{x} = 8 \times 14 = 112$$

Subtract the sum of the 7 known scores:
$$\text{Known sum} = 11 + 13 + 15 + 12 + 16 + 14 + 16 = 97$$
$$\text{Missing score} = 112 - 97 = 15$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate the total of all 8 scores as 8 * 14 = 112 and sum the 7 known scores as 97.
Subtract to obtain the eighth score: 112 - 97 = 15.

hints: Do not average the two means directly; find the sum of each group first: $8 \times 14.5$ and $12 \times 17.0$.
Add the two totals together and divide by the total number of items: $8 + 12 = 20$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the sum for each group and the overall total:
$$\sum x_A = 8 \times 14.5 = 116,\quad \sum x_B = 12 \times 17.0 = 204$$
$$\sum x_{\text{combined}} = 116 + 204 = 320$$

Divide by the total count of 20 items:
$$\bar{x}_{\text{combined}} = \frac{320}{20} = 16$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Multiply each mean by its group count:
$$116 + 204 = 320$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate group totals: 8 * 14.5 = 116 and 12 * 17.0 = 204, giving combined total 320.
Divide by total frequency (20) to obtain combined mean = 320 / 20 = 16.

hints: The midpoint of any class $[a, b)$ is given by $\frac{a + b}{2}$.
Notice that the first three classes have width $10$, but the last class spans from $30$ to $50$ (width $20$).

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the midpoint formula $\frac{a+b}{2}$ for each interval:
$$x_1 = \frac{0+10}{2} = 5,\quad x_2 = \frac{10+20}{2} = 15,\quad x_3 = \frac{20+30}{2} = 25,\quad x_4 = \frac{30+50}{2} = 40$$

Explain the calculation for the unequal interval:
$$\text{Class width is } 50 - 30 = 20 \implies \text{Midpoint} = 30 + \frac{20}{2} = 40$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that the last class has unequal width of 20 (from 30 to 50), so its midpoint is (30 + 50) / 2 = 40.

hints: The frequency of an interval is found by subtracting the previous cumulative frequency from the current cumulative frequency.

walkthrough.text:
Subtract consecutive cumulative frequencies:
$$f_1 = 6$$
$$f_2 = 15 - 6 = 9$$
$$f_3 = 27 - 15 = 12$$
$$f_4 = 32 - 27 = 5$$

Verify that the sum of class frequencies equals the final cumulative total:
$$\sum f = 6 + 9 + 12 + 5 = 32$$

hints: Consider what happens to the exact numbers when data is grouped into classes.
We assume every item in a class is equal to the midpoint, which is an approximation.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the loss of granular information in grouped data:
$$\text{Grouping conceals the exact numerical values of the individual observations.}$$

Explain the midpoint assumption:
$$\text{All } f \text{ observations in an interval are represented by one single value (the midpoint } x_m\text{).}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State loss of raw values:
$$\text{Exact raw values inside intervals are unknown}$$

Explain midpoint approximation:
$$\text{Assuming all items equal the midpoint introduces an estimate}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State that the individual raw data values within each class interval are unknown.
Explain that all observations in a class are approximated by the class midpoint, which may differ from their actual values.

hints: Total height of group 1 is $9 \times 168\text{ cm}$.
Total height of group 2 is $11 \times 174\text{ cm}$. Add the two totals together.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate total height for each squad:
$$\text{Squad 1: } 9 \times 168 = 1512\text{ cm},\quad \text{Squad 2: } 11 \times 174 = 1914\text{ cm}$$

Add both totals:
$$\text{Total height} = 1512 + 1914 = 3426\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate totals for both squads: 9 * 168 = 1512 cm and 11 * 174 = 1914 cm.
Sum the totals to obtain combined height = 1512 + 1914 = 3426 cm.

hints: Divide your total from part (a) by $20$.
Compare the number of players in each group ($11$ vs $9$) to explain the weighting.

walkthrough.text:
Divide the combined total by the total number of players:
$$\bar{x}_{\text{combined}} = \frac{3426}{20} = 171.3\text{ cm}$$

Explain why the mean is skewed towards 174 cm:
$$\text{The second group carries more weight since } 11 > 9, \text{ pulling the mean past the midpoint 171.0 to 171.3 cm.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Explain weighting:
$$\text{Larger group (11 vs 9) pulls the mean closer to 174 cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that the second squad is larger (11 players > 9 players), giving greater weight to 174 cm.

hints: Use $\text{Midpoint} = \frac{\text{Lower} + \text{Upper}}{2}$ for each row.
Be careful with the final class $[30, 50)$, whose width is $20$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate midpoints for the equal width intervals:
$$x_1 = \frac{0+10}{2} = 5,\quad x_2 = \frac{10+20}{2} = 15,\quad x_3 = \frac{20+30}{2} = 25$$

Calculate midpoint for the wider interval:
$$x_4 = \frac{30+50}{2} = 40$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify midpoints of first three classes: 5, 15, 25.

hints: Multiply each frequency by its corresponding midpoint from part (a) to calculate $f \times x$.
Add the products together to find $\sum f x$, then divide by the total frequency $\sum f = 20$.

walkthrough.text:
Sum the products to obtain $\sum f x$:
$$\sum f x = 20 + 105 + 125 + 160 = 410$$

Divide by $\sum f = 20$ to estimate the mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum f x}{\sum f} = \frac{410}{20} = 20.5\text{ minutes}$$

hints: Total cost is the number of items multiplied by the mean cost per item.
The number of items is $10$ and the mean cost is $7.20\text{ dollars}$.
Compute $10 \times 7.20 = 72.00\text{ dollars}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the total formula:
$$\text{Total cost} = n \times \bar{x} = 10 \times 7.20\text{ dollars}$$

Evaluate the total expenditure:
$$\text{Total cost} = 72.00\text{ dollars}$$

hints: Calculate the cost of the 6 notebooks: $6 \times 4.50 = 27.00\text{ dollars}$.
Add the cost of notebooks ($27$), the bag ($21$), and the 3 folders ($3x$) to set up the equation equal to $72$.
Solve $3x + 48 = 72$ for $x$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the known item expenditures:
$$\text{Notebooks: } 6 \times 4.50 = 27.00\text{ dollars},\quad \text{Bag: } 21.00\text{ dollars}$$
$$\text{Known sum} = 27.00 + 21.00 = 48.00\text{ dollars}$$

Set up the linear equation for the 3 folders:
$$3x + 48.00 = 72.00$$

Solve for the cost of one folder $x$:
$$3x = 72.00 - 48.00 = 24.00 \implies x = 8.00\text{ dollars}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solve for x: 3x = 24, so x = 8.00 dollars.

hints: Find the midpoint of each interval using $\frac{\text{Lower} + \text{Upper}}{2}$.
Multiply each class frequency by its midpoint and sum the four products to find $\sum f x$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the class midpoints:
$$x_1 = 25,\quad x_2 = 40,\quad x_3 = 65,\quad x_4 = 90$$

Calculate each weighted contribution $f x$:
$$f_1 x_1 = 6 \times 25 = 150,\quad f_2 x_2 = 12 \times 40 = 480$$
$$f_3 x_3 = 7 \times 65 = 455,\quad f_4 x_4 = 5 \times 90 = 450$$

Sum the contributions:
$$\sum f x = 150 + 480 + 455 + 450 = 1535$$

hints: Divide $\sum f x = 1535$ by the total frequency $30$.
Compare $48\text{ g}$ with the midpoint used ($40\text{ g}$).
If the true values are larger than the midpoint, the estimated mean underestimates the actual mean.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the grouped mean estimate:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum f x}{\sum f} = \frac{1535}{30} = 51.166... \approx 51.2\text{ g (3 s.f.)}$$

Compare the actual values ($48\text{ g}$) with the class midpoint ($40\text{ g}$):
$$\text{Actual value } 48 > 40 = \text{Midpoint}$$

Deduce the effect on the estimate:
$$\text{Because the true values in that class exceed the midpoint, the calculated estimate underestimates the true mean.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Conclude underestimation:
$$\text{The estimate is an underestimate of the true mean}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that if the actual values in class 30 <= x < 50 were near 48 g, they exceed the midpoint 40 g, so the true mean would be higher than the estimate (the estimate underestimates the true mean).

hints: Subtract consecutive cumulative totals to find each frequency: $8$, $20-8$, $44-20$, $50-44$.
The four resulting class frequencies are $8$, $12$, $24$, and $6$.
Calculate the midpoint of each interval: $\frac{0+20}{2} = 10$, $\frac{20+30}{2} = 25$, $\frac{30+50}{2} = 40$, $\frac{50+80}{2} = 65$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the individual class frequencies:
$$f_1 = 8,\quad f_2 = 20 - 8 = 12,\quad f_3 = 44 - 20 = 24,\quad f_4 = 50 - 44 = 6$$

Calculate the class midpoints:
$$x_1 = \frac{0+20}{2} = 10,\quad x_2 = \frac{20+30}{2} = 25,\quad x_3 = \frac{30+50}{2} = 40,\quad x_4 = \frac{50+80}{2} = 65$$

hints: Multiply each frequency by its midpoint: $8(10)$, $12(25)$, $24(40)$, $6(65)$.
Add the four products together to get $\sum f x = 1730$.
Divide by the total number of journeys ($50$).

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the weighted midpoint products:
$$8(10) = 80,\quad 12(25) = 300,\quad 24(40) = 960,\quad 6(65) = 390$$

Compute the sum of products:
$$\sum f x = 80 + 300 + 960 + 390 = 1730$$

Calculate the estimated mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum f x}{\sum f} = \frac{1730}{50} = 34.6\text{ minutes}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Divide by 50 to obtain estimated mean = 1730 / 50 = 34.6 minutes.

hints: Multiply each class size by its respective mean score.
Add the three products together to obtain the overall total score.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the sum of scores for each class:
$$\sum x_1 = 25 \times 64.0 = 1600$$
$$\sum x_2 = 35 \times 72.0 = 2520$$
$$\sum x_3 = 40 \times 68.5 = 2740$$

Add the three sums together:
$$\sum x_{\text{total}} = 1600 + 2520 + 2740 = 6860$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Multiply n by mean for each class:
$$1600,\; 2520,\; 2740$$

hints: Divide your total of $6860$ by the total student count of $100$.
Compute the unweighted average: $\frac{64 + 72 + 68.5}{3} \approx 68.17$.
Explain that the unweighted average assumes all classes have equal size, which is false.
Class 3 ($40$ students) and Class 2 ($35$ students) are much larger than Class 1 ($25$ students).

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the weighted combined mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{6860}{100} = 68.6$$

Evaluate the unweighted average of the three means:
$$\frac{64.0 + 72.0 + 68.5}{3} = \frac{204.5}{3} \approx 68.17$$

Explain why the unweighted average fails:
$$\text{The three classes have unequal cohort sizes (25, 35, 40). An unweighted average gives equal weight (33.3%) to each class, ignoring that 40% of the students belong to Class 3.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Explain weighting:
$$\text{Classes are unequal in size, so each student must carry equal weight}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that the classes have unequal sizes (25, 35, 40), so larger classes must have proportionally greater weighting in the overall mean.

hints: First change: $66 - 58 = +8$. Second change: $64 - 70 = -6$.
Net change to the total score is $+8 - 6 = +2$.
New total is $6860 + 2 = 6862$.
Divide by $100$ to get the new mean: $68.62$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the net effect of the mark adjustments on the total sum:
$$\Delta = (66 - 58) + (64 - 70) = +8 - 6 = +2\text{ marks}$$

Update the grand total:
$$\sum x_{\text{new}} = 6860 + 2 = 6862$$

Compute the new combined mean:
$$\bar{x}_{\text{new}} = \frac{6862}{100} = 68.62\text{ (or 68.6 to 3 s.f.)}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate new combined mean = 6862 / 100 = 68.62 (or 68.6 to 3 s.f.).

hints: The sum of all frequencies must equal the total number of students ($80$).
Compute the midpoint $\frac{\text{Lower}+\text{Upper}}{2}$ for each class: $10, 30, 50, 80$.
Note that the last class spans from $60$ to $100$, so its midpoint is $\frac{60+100}{2} = 80$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the equation for total frequency:
$$14 + 26 + k + 16 = 80$$
$$56 + k = 80 \implies k = 24$$

Determine the midpoint of each class interval:
$$x_1 = \frac{0+20}{2} = 10,\quad x_2 = \frac{20+40}{2} = 30,\quad x_3 = \frac{40+60}{2} = 50,\quad x_4 = \frac{60+100}{2} = 80$$

Confirm complete frequency distribution:
$$\text{Frequencies: } [14,\; 26,\; 24,\; 16],\quad \text{Midpoints: } [10,\; 30,\; 50,\; 80]$$

ai_rubric.observable: Set up total frequency equation: 14 + 26 + k + 16 = 80.

hints: Multiply each frequency by its midpoint: $14(10)$, $26(30)$, $24(50)$, $16(80)$.
Add the products together to find $\sum f x = 3400$.
Divide $\sum f x$ by $80$ to find the estimated mean.
Verify: $\frac{3400}{80} = 42.5\text{ marks}$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute each product $f x$:
$$14 \times 10 = 140,\quad 26 \times 30 = 780,\quad 24 \times 50 = 1200,\quad 16 \times 80 = 1280$$

Sum the products to obtain $\sum f x$:
$$\sum f x = 140 + 780 + 1200 + 1280 = 3400$$

Divide by the total frequency $N = 80$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{3400}{80} = 42.5\text{ marks}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Divide by 80 to obtain estimated mean = 3400 / 80 = 42.5 marks.

hints: Moving from $[20, 40)$ to $[40, 60)$ changes the midpoints assigned to these $5$ students from $30$ to $50$.
Each of the $5$ students gains $50 - 30 = 20$ in the weighted sum $\sum f x$.
Total increase in $\sum f x$ is $5 \times 20 = 100$.
Divide this increase by $80$ to find the change in the estimated mean: $\frac{100}{80} = +1.25\text{ marks}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the shift in class frequencies:
$$\text{Frequency of } [20, 40) \text{ becomes } 26 - 5 = 21$$
$$\text{Frequency of } [40, 60) \text{ becomes } 24 + 5 = 29$$

Calculate the change in $\sum f x$:
$$\Delta \sum f x = 5 \times (x_3 - x_2) = 5 \times (50 - 30) = 5 \times 20 = +100$$

Calculate the resulting change in the estimated mean:
$$\Delta \bar{x} = \frac{\Delta \sum f x}{N} = \frac{100}{80} = +1.25\text{ marks}$$
$$\bar{x}_{\text{new}} = 42.5 + 1.25 = 43.75\text{ marks}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Note boundary shift:
$$5 \text{ students move from midpoint 30 to midpoint 50}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that the 5 students cross the class boundary from [20, 40) into [40, 60), decreasing the frequency of [20, 40) by 5 and increasing [40, 60) by 5.
Calculate change in sum(fx): 5 students shift from midpoint 30 to midpoint 50, so delta sum(fx) = 5 * (50 - 30) = +100.
Calculate increase in estimated mean: 100 / 80 = +1.25 marks (giving new estimated mean = 43.75 marks).
